Guidance & outlook: For FY27, we continue to expect capex of approximately INR 250 crore to INR 300 crore.
During Q1 FY27, our consolidated revenue from operations stood at INR 1,033 crore from INR 887* crore, registering a healthy growth of 16.4% year-on-year.
Q1 FY27 Earnings Call Page 4 of 17 145 crore, a growth of 44% year-on-year.
Growth & demand: Starting with wire ropes - Value growth was strong at 18% year-on-year even as overall volumes were marginally lower.
In the domestic market, rope volumes grew approximately 12% year-on-year, while value grew around 21%, supported by healthy demand across crane, elevator and fishing segments.
Now turning to wires - The business delivered healthy growth during the quarter with volumes up approximately 19% and revenue growing around 32% year-on-year.
Margins & costs: Operating EBITDA stood at INR 208 crore, a 44% increase year-on-year with an EBITDA margin of 20.1%.
Together with improvement in product mix, cost discipline and operating efficiencies, this enabled us to expand EBITDA margins to 20.1%.

Even after the input cost increase, we were able to sort of pass on the input cost, and then further still improve our product mix as well as manage our costs on a year-on- year basis to get these overall margins.
Capex & expansion: During the quarter, we incurred capital expenditure of approximately INR 73 crore.
After funding capex of INR 73 crore, free cash flow stood at INR 135 crore.

So, as we guided earlier, about INR 250 crore to INR 300 crore would be the capex, including routine capex or maintenance capex on a yearly basis for us to be able to continue with the topline growth of 10% to 12% in terms of volume and around 15% on value.
Balance sheet & cash: We generated operating cash flow of approximately INR 242 crore, representing cash conversion of 116% of operating EBITDA and closed the quarter with a net cash position of approximately INR 465 crore.
This demonstrates that our profitability growth has been driven by a richer product mix, effective cost recovery and strong operating leverage, enabling a significant expansion in earnings.
Our operating cash flow before tax stood at INR 242 crore, translating into a cash conversion of approximately 116% of operating EBITDA.
Risks & challenges: I want to highlight that the volume decline was largely due to the Middle East operations.
Now coming to the Middle East operations, - volumes were down approximately 28% due to continued geopolitical and market disruptions.
Firstly, as we mentioned in the opening remarks as well, volumes came in lower in the Middle East, which declined around 28% due to the ongoing geopolitical conflict.

So looking at the current opportunities globally, including the domestic market, we feel and we still maintain that we will be able to get to 10% to 12% growth of volume in this financial year.

So, as we guided earlier, about INR 250 crore to INR 300 crore would be the capex, including routine capex or maintenance capex on a yearly basis for us to be able to continue with the topline growth of 10% to 12% in terms of volume and around 15% on value.
Our goal would be to maintain margins upward of 20% whereas the focus would be on both absolute topline and bottom-line growth.
